    A Origin

    OSCILLA began with a simple question: how much of an acoustic laboratory could live entirely inside a web browser?

    The first version was deliberately direct:

    1. Generate
    2. Hear
    3. See
    4. Inspect

    From there it grew into a denser instrument for frequency, phase, modulation, filtering, sequencing and microphone comparison, without hiding the signal path.

    B Engineering

    The speed was unusual. The constraints were deliberately not.

    • Deterministic The same source builds the same bytes; the committed file is the deployed file.
    • Protected V1 engine schedules are frozen and replayed; a browser gate runs Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
    • Verified The interface is compared against a visual reference.
    • Recorded Architecture decisions are written down with their reasons.
    • Honest Approximation is never presented as measurement; relative is not calibrated.

    C Method

    Much of the implementation was AI-assisted. That is how OSCILLA is built, not why it exists.

    1. Human judgment defined the product and the architecture.
    2. AI accelerated implementation.
    3. Majordomus constrained, organised and verified the process.
    4. The repository remained the source of truth.

    Engineering system

    Majordomus

    A repository-native engineering control plane for human and AI contributors.

    Instead of depending on an AI conversation to remember how the project should work, the repository carries its own machine-readable engineering context. Every contributor, person or model, starts from the same rules, plan and evidence and finishes against the same checks.

    • Architectural rules
    • Repository context
    • Task scope
    • Plans & milestones
    • Implementation evidence
    • Use-case coverage
    • Workflows
    • Worktree discipline
    • Verification

    AI accelerated implementation.
    Majordomus supplied structure, memory and constraints.
    The repository remained the source of truth.

    majordomus.dev (opens in a new tab)

    D Two experiments

    OSCILLA explores sound and frequency. Its development explores a narrower question: can implementation speed rise without architecture, verification and product identity dissolving around it?

    The measurement tooling has shipped as Measure and Experiments, and composition and signal flow as Studio.

    Save preset

    Stored in this browser (localStorage, preset schema v1). The continuous-playback permission is never stored.

    Headphones required

    Binaural beats need one tone per ear: put on headphones and keep the level low before you continue. Speakers mix both channels and the effect disappears.

    Config link

    The clipboard is not available here. Copy the link manually; opening it restores these settings and never starts playback.

    Keyboard shortcuts

    Space (hold)
    Hold to play (programmed patterns: trigger)
    Enter on Hold / Trigger
    Trigger once
    Esc
    Stop immediately; close menus and dialogs
    ← → on tabs and segments
    Move and select
    PgUp / PgDn on the frequency slider
    One octave up / down
    Sequencer timeline: arrows, Alt+arrows, Del, Ctrl/⌘+D
    Select, move, delete, duplicate blocks

    Space does nothing while a text field, button or dialog has focus. Start at a low level: OSCILLA caps the logical gain at 0.25 and, unless continuous playback is allowed in Device & Limits, stops every tone after the hard limit.

    Microphone

    The microphone starts only when you press “Use microphone”. Echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain are requested off, so the analyser sees the raw input. Audio never leaves this page.

    Detected frequencies come from the FFT peak (parabolic interpolation; autocorrelation below 1 kHz) and are never shown finer than the bin resolution. Use the Compare tab for freeze, averaging and peak hold.

    Not a calibrated measurement. From file:// some browsers refuse the microphone; the panel then says so.

    Settings

    Hard limit (Device & Limits): scheduled on the audio clock, so it holds even if the page stalls. It also caps the Finite tone. Other programmed patterns stop at their own end (max 30 s); a continuous sweep repeat needs “Allow continuous playback”.

    Browser: · Platform: · Audio:

    Level calibration

    Put a known external acoustic reference on the microphone (typically a calibrator that produces 94 dB re 20 µPa at 1 kHz), switch it on and capture it here. OSCILLA reads its level through the same input as a measurement; the offset is the reference minus the reading. It is valid only for this microphone, input gain, browser settings and position: OSCILLA records the input and stops applying the calibration when the input changes.
